page.layout: One printed page: a narrow blank column on the left, with the page number 104 in a box at the top; beside it a single text column of large roman type, running down the page, with a hanging quotation mark at the start of many lines. No running head, no catchword or signature in this part.; One column of running text on the left printed page, with the running head above it. Right of it, the edge of the next printed page shows as a narrow sliver of one column, too cut to read.

main_text.p: Sed paulò ulterius filum Historiæ rosequamur. Hoc ipso tempore mar-urium passus est fortissimus ille Christi athleta Ecclesiæ Affricanæ lumen & co-imen D. Cyprianus; qui in Epistola rima ad Cornelium Episcopum Roma-num, in hunc modum scribit; [Re-tusus aduersarius, adunati exercitus, fide pariter & vigore intellexit, Christi milites vigilare iam sobrios,& armatos ad prælium stare, vinci non posse, mori posse: & hoc ipso inuict-os esse, quia mori non timent, nec repugnare contra impugnantes cū occidere innocentibus ne nocentem licet; sed promptè & animas & san-guinè tradere, ut cū sæuitia & malitia grassetur, à malis & sæuis velociùs recedatur.] In quæ Cypriani verba Romana Editio cum Priuilegio Pÿ Quarti, Typis Pauli Manutij impressa hanc in fine libri assuit glossam; [Loquitur de Christianis illius temporis, iussu impiorum Tyrannorum apprehendis, vel iam apprehensis, & vi tormentorum ad sacrificandum Idolis fide abnegata cogendis: qui licet ad

page.notes: The opening lines are large type and show only their first letters; the hanging quotation marks are the only legible marks on the lines below them. The "m" and "&" lines are single letters, doubtful as to what follows. Right-edge sliver not legible; no text transcribed from it. Words at the left edge are cut and given as they appear (rosequamur, urium, thleta, imen).
